title: 5 Years After the Fall: Why the World Still Misreads the Taliban
author: Munera Yousufzada
text:
Armed fighters of the Taliban in Kabul, Aug. 17 2021.
Credit: Screenshot/ VOA
Five years have passed since the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan. During this period, the international community tried a wide range of policies to influence the Taliban’s behavior, from humanitarian assistance and political and economic pressure to diplomatic engagement and negotiations that began through indirect channels and, today, in some cases, have developed into direct talks. At the same time, human rights defenders, political opponents of the Taliban, and many ordinary Afghans did not abandon their resistance. From street protests and underground schools to human rights campaigns and various forms of civil disobedience, they sought to prevent the normalization of Taliban rule both within Afghanistan and internationally.[...]
